newsitem.title: USA: Goodyear tire settles patent suit.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear tire settles patent suit.

text.p: The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co on Monday said it settled a patent infringement suit it filed in 1993 against Contentinental General Fire and later against Germany's Continental AG.
The suit had charged Continental General with infringement of Goodyear patents on its Aquatred tire, a Goodyear official said in statement.
Continental acknowledged in a consent decree its Hydro 2000 tire infringed two utility patents and one design patent that protected features of Goodyear's Aquatred tire.

"After Goodyear filed suit, the Patent and Trademark Office conducted a reexamination of one of our utility patents and on April 30, 1996, confirmed its validity. Following the confirmation, Continental General dropped all its counterclaims and entered settlement discussions with Goodyear," Richard Steichen, Goodyear's vice president of world technology said in a statement.
Continental General agreed to destroy all its Hydro 2000 tire molds and to pay an undisclosed amount of damages, Goodyear said.
The comany also agreed not to to contest Goodyear's Aquatred patents' enforceability and validity in subsequent litigation.
Continental AG, the parent corporation, entered into a separate agreement acknowledging the Hydro 2000 tire infringed certain Aquatred U.S. patents.
